summary.name: Database of Databases
summary.one_liner: A curated online encyclopedia cataloguing database management system implementations, from Carnegie Mellon University.
use_cases: Finding a database system to fit a data model
Researching database history and discontinued systems
summary.what_it_does: The site is a curated reference guide listing implementations of database systems. It lets visitors browse entries by data model, such as key-value, graph, document/XML, relational, and array/matrix, with 14 models listed. It highlights a featured system (currently ScyllaDB, described as an open-source distributed wide-column NoSQL database) and shows leaderboards of most recently modified, most viewed, and most edited entries. It also includes collections such as recently deceased databases and database systems developed by Amazon or CWI.
notable: Leaderboards of most viewed, most edited, and recently modified entries
Includes a section on recently deceased and historical databases
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page; the 'free' value is inferred from it being a public reference site and should be treated as unknown.
Entries are community-curated reference listings, not a tool for running databases.
